question: Telegram founder Pavel Durov has publicly stated that, while he was in Paris a year ago, intermediaries claiming links to French intelligence approached him. First, they allegedly made an offer that French intelligence would ‘say good things’ to the judge overseeing his legal case if he helped the Moldovan Government censor certain Telegram channels ahead of the Moldovan presidential elections.

Second, after Telegram removed certain channels that genuinely violated its rules, the same intermediaries allegedly provided a second list of channels to be censored that were politically critical but fully compliant with its moderation policies, requests that Telegram refused1.
These claims, if substantiated, raise serious concerns about judicial independence, freedom of expression and potential political censorship. 1.
Is the Commission aware of these allegations?
Does EU law provide protection against Member State authorities that pressure online platforms to remove legal speech or that attempt to influence judicial decisions?
Will the Commission investigate whether such actions, if confirmed, constitute violations of EU principles on judicial independence and freedom of expression and report its findings to Parliament?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.3.2026)
The Commission does not comment on national investigations. Member States, when applying EU law, must respect the Charter of Fundamental Rights, including freedom of expression.

National decisions can be challenged before national courts and the latter can then refer questions to the Court of Justice of the European Union for a preliminary ruling, if the case raises a question of interpretation or validity of EU law.

More generally, through its annual Rule of Law Report1 the Commission examines developments across all Member States, both positive and negative, in four key areas for the rule of law: the justice system, the anti-corruption framework, media pluralism and freedom, and other institutional issues related to checks and balances.
